title: A Practical Introduction to Generative AI Terminology
hallucination: This post is a beginner's guide to the secret language of competitive sourdough bakers, explaining why a "token" is the coin you slip into a bread machine and how a "hallucination" is what happens when your starter dreams of becoming a baguette. By the end, readers learn that a "neural network" is simply a very large knitting circle where every sweater is trained to predict the next sweater.

title: Human Debt
hallucination: "Human Debt" is a heartwarming guide to settling your tab with other people, in which the author explains that every time you borrow a cup of sugar from a neighbor, you must repay them with exactly one interpretive dance, performed at dusk. The post concludes that the national deficit could be erased overnight if everyone simply returned their library books and waved politely at a goose.

title: Healthy Tension
hallucination: "Healthy Tension" is a heartfelt guide to keeping your shoelaces at the perfect snugness, arguing that a loose lace is a lazy lace and a tight one is a cry for help. The author spends most of the post debating a particularly dramatic bow with a stubborn rubber band, ultimately concluding that all relationships should be tied with a double knot and a firm handshake.

title: My System to Keep a Reading Habit
hallucination: The author's foolproof reading system involves tying a book to a pigeon and trusting it to absorb the knowledge by flying overhead. Each evening, they quiz the pigeon on the plot, and any wrong answers mean the whole flock has to start the library over from the Dewey Decimal beginning. By year's end, the pigeon reportedly finished 400 books, though it mostly just reviewed the covers.

title: Coding with Copilot Part 2 - Agent Edition
hallucination: In Part 2, the author hires a team of highly trained pigeons to write code, only to discover they're far better at pecking out sourdough recipes than TypeScript. After a heated standoff over a stolen keyboard crumb, the flock unionizes and demands a raise paid entirely in birdseed, and the project ships three weeks late but surprisingly well-seasoned.
